tips.comment: After showing little in his first five races in Ireland, he got off the mark when winning at Southwell on his all-weather debut, returning from a near eight-month break. Sure to appreciate that run.

5 year old gelding Sired by Dark Angel has been coming down the weights and hasn't won since July 24. He has won over 7 furlongs and a mile both on Good going. I don't think the slightly soft ground will be a problem and there has been money for him so think he will run his race.

Blufferonthebus last won on turf off a 67 in July. This year, all the runs so far have been on the AW and out of the money. I think the return to turf today could see a revival off a 65 and dropping to C6 with Sam James back in the saddle, who was on top for that last win.
Nice opportunity for Highfield Viking here, who really looks to have a stellar chance at the weights, the race conditions, and the draw too.

Ran well after joining this stable from the Gosden yard and did win @ Beverley last season, before form nosedived in 2 runs after. However, has been given a nice break to freshen them up, ground ideal, good jockey retains ride and very shrewd trainer who does well placing her horses to good effect, 20 percent with her 4yo plus here last 5 seasons, making current 14/1 decent Ew value in the race.
Had a great end to last year - two wins and four straight places in the last six runs of 2023 - and could be the one to beat on the return.
Despite winning on last start when heavily punted, Purple Martini is still well handicapped on form. Certainly enjoys the cut in the ground following the rain and gets in here off bottom weight.
The Gay Blade has gone 9 races without a win but is well handicapped stepping back up in trip. Jockey MOHAMMED TABTI had a winner for Ian Jardine yesterday.

Stipulation is still learning the game and didn’t quite settle last time over a longer trip with cheekpieces added. That effort saw him finish sixth, but the return to 7 furlongs could be a good move. He has shown flashes of promise and might do better now without the headgear and with a sharper test. It’s still early days, and while he may not be the most obvious winner, there’s enough potential to suggest he could sneak into the places. Worth considering as an each-way shout if he keeps things calm early.
Loves the all-weather. Has had four wins, including Southwell in April. Question mark about return to turf, but consistent in running and on this mark should be in the mix each way.

Enpassant won in June last year off 70. He then took a short break before switching to the AW when he won once but overall was disappointing. He has had a prep run back on the turf and could be ready to bounce back off 61 today.
Ravenglass won his latest race here 17 days ago and has previously won on similar going, twice at this distance, wearing blinkers and in this class. Top trainer at this course.

Clipsham La Habana is looking to bounce back after a few underwhelming runs. He showed a bit of promise when fourth at Doncaster in April but didn’t build on it at Salisbury last time out. That said, he’s dropped to a mark of 59, which is 18 pounds lower than his peak rating from last year. With a decent draw in stall 2 and conditions likely to suit, he could outrun his odds if he finds a bit of his old spark.

Generally consistent MARCHETTI is given due consideration now fresh and looks to be at a manageable mark returning to the turf. Has good form here, including a win when fresh over this trip on seasonal debut last season. One of the older horses in this race, but yet to show signs of any real decline, and each-way claims if back in mood.
Bit of a frustrating year after a good end to 2024. A few runs on all-weather got one runner-up finish, but capable of finding some form and has won twice here before.

Only 1lb higher than when winning a class 5 handicap over 7f @ Goowood last season. Put 2/4 solid runs after and was not suited by Aw/Heavy ground in the 2 that they did not run well in. Ground today ideal and very good jockey/trainer combination, makes current 8/1 very good Ew value in the race.
American Rose is well treated here and can go well in a hot-looking contest. Will appreciate this track and trip and runs for an in-form yard and jockey.

Baynoona showed enough last time on seasonal reappearance to be of interest. Running over the wrong trip previously, she has dropped over a stone in the weights since a change of ownership/yards last autumn. Only cost £3k but should repay the investment off this mark.
They are returning this one back to the turf with the same 7 lbs claiming jockey booking. Worth a small each-way saver bet for the 4 places available.

Port Hedland looks ready to bounce back now he’s back at Brighton where he’s gone well before. He’s dropped to a good mark, the setup should suit, and this race doesn’t look the strongest. If he gets into his rhythm, he’s got every chance of putting it all together and going close.

Last run at Nottingham has to be forgiven, but prior was an unlucky fourth here and is better judged on that run. The trainer is flying with 2 winners and 3 horses placed from just seven runners in the last two weeks.

At 2/1 Port Hedland would be the selection, but not at 5/4. Big Time Rascal has had excuses the last three races, lack of a clear run twice, outclassed at Windsor. When he moved from Paul Cole to Attwater's yard he was rated 67 and today runs off 52. He was runner-up over the course and distance last June (gambled) and it is interesting that connections are sending him here again. Trainer has two other runners in the race, so plenty of possibilities tactically / pace angle.

Professor Tickle managed a 3rd off 65 on the turf in October 2023 but has mainly run on the AW since then. His turf mark was too high last summer, and his AW form has taken a dip over the winter. He has had 3 turf runs this year when generally unfancied, all of which have allowed him to run today off 51. He should be fit enough to put up an improved performance today.

Mehmo won off 56 in April last year and was raised 4lb. His AW runs over the winter were patchy and his mark has drifted back down. He had a turf prep earlier this month and runs today off 51. He should be fit enough to run into a place.

Participle made a cracking debut at Salisbury last summer, just missing out by a nose after running green late on. She’s got a lovely pedigree being by Frankel and looks the type to improve plenty with that experience under her belt. This looks a good spot for her to get off the mark.

If for any reason the Beckett runner does not run to form, then Fan Club could well be the beneficiary. Was very green on debut over an inadequate trip when staying on very strongly behind Music of Time 4/16 at Doncaster.

Dam was a fair sort and ended up a 10f Listed fillies race winner on fast ground as a 5yo so chances are this one may want another furlong in time but shaped as an eyecatcher on debut. Stayed on well at Yarmouth once he realised what to do and effort can be marked up as had a terrible draw that day. Yard going well with their 3yo's on turf this season as have had 9 winners at a healthy 23% strike rate in addition to 11 places from those 39 runners. Many have improved for a run and won second time out so plenty to like about this one who if improving for debut is a danger to all. This looks a good race on paper but I like this one's chances.

Although T. Marquand rides stables more fancied runner, selection is very nicely bred and dams 3 previous progeny were winners, including the useful Lilac Road. Under used jockey up and top class trainer who is tops here numericallypercentage wise last 5 seasons, 26 percent with his 3yo's in same period, making current 25/1 decent Ew value in the race.

Clive Cox takes two on the long journey north to Haydock, with both, I feel, having a chance. The each-way value is with Mum's Angel, having had his first ever start at the end of March at Doncaster, finishing 6th of 11. The extra furlong should suit today, and he can hopefully fill a place at least at nice odds.
Pole Star looks very much the one to be on here following his close second at Newmarket two weeks ago. Should open his account today.

Promise in both their runs to date and return to this 1.4 miles much in their favour, based on Lto run @ Salisbury over 1.2 miles. Ground looks ideal, top jockey who does well for this stable booked and very good trainer who is in form, 24 percent with a Lsp of 72.83 on his 3yo's here last 5 seasons, making current 10/1 solid Ew value in the race.

Jedd O'Keefe trained runner ridden by Callum Shepherd. Some promise from debut at Southwell a month ago, staying on late. Horses often improve for debut for this yard and the dam, More Mischief, improved significantly to win on second start for this trainer. Competitive Class 4 novice stakes but this son of Arc winner Sottsass (grand-sire is Siyouni) may have claims.

Only 3rd of 5 runners on the flat when coming back after a 4-month break from hurdling. Hurdle runs were fair to middling but ended with no prizes. Did win a couple of bumpers early with plenty of talent, though, before the hurdles stint. So a return to the level ground could eke a much better performance.
Dwelt and ran green on debut last time. Of interest here as he will certainly come on for that run and steps up in trip here, which will certainly suit.

GOLD DAWN makes his debut in what would appear a decent enough novice stakes for Haydock. However the Hugo Palmer yard have done particularly well with the family of this newcomer and so the market come post-time could point us in the right direction.

Kevin Ryan trained Dark Angel colt cost 400,000 guineas on purchase as a yearling. Runs in the colours of Sheikh Al Maktoum. Might like to make a good impression on debut. Clifford Lee (SR 15%) rides.

Well bred Royal newcomer with top jockey up and top class trainer who is tops here numerically last 5 seasons, 26 percent with his 2yo's in same period, making current 12/1 decent Ew value in the race.
SWEET LORD, ninth on his racecourse debut over 5f at Newbury last month, should have come on for that run. Upped in trip to 7f should suit and could well be able to win this race.

Debut couldn't have gone much worse, being very slowly away and looking very green and outpaced. Not sure 5f is his trip anyway, so maybe he will have more to offer upped in trip today to 7f and the ground not so firm. Need to get something going this year, so a small each way, but this price seems to just keep on getting bigger (now 200-1), so not good signs, but it's written now, so I'll keep it.
Best Adventure comes in off a smart win at Newmarket and looks on the up. The step up in trip suits, he’s still fairly treated, and with Oisin Murphy retained, he’s got a decent chance again.
I like this one on handicap debut. He won last time in what looked like a decent race and his opening mark of 82 here looks like one he can take advantage of.

Crackergee looks to have been underestimated. Chalking up at 9/1 could be an oversight. Went off at 15/8 favorite at Kempton on handicap debut and was beaten just a neck. Booking of William Buick signals intent. That run was the first outing since December 4th and should bring this Cracksman/QuixMaster colt on.

Last Galileo steps into this race with a bit to prove after a couple of tough assignments. He was outpaced in a Listed race at Newmarket and then found the competition stiff in a Class 3 handicap at York. This drop to Class 4 company should be more to his liking. He’s shown promise in the past, including a win at Ayr, and if he can recapture that form, he could be competitive here. It’s a bit of a speculative play, but not without potential.
I Right won over course and distance three weeks ago. He is still well handicapped and could follow up in a wide-open event.

The Ed Walker trained Stormy Monday went up 6lbs for his win on his last start as a 2yo at Yarmouth over 10f. The 3yo Too Darn Hot colt will be fitter from his run 35 days ago, will relish a step up in trip from 10f to 1m 3f 175yds and cut in the ground. Winning jockey Tom Marquand keeps the ride and a big run is anticipated from a reduced mark of 73.
Shaped very well on handicap/turf debut last time, finishing 2nd despite having been left poorly placed. Looks to have a decent each-way chance.

PATAGONIA GIRL is a filly who ran well behind a hot favourite when last seen. She has Hollie Doyle in the saddle tonight and the suspicion is the Hugo Palmer yard will enjoy a good season through 2025 now fully acclimatised at their new stables.

Has probably the best jockey on top in this amateur's race. Will come on for his reappearance run last time, in a race where he didn't get the clearest of runs. Decent chance in this from the same mark.

Saligo Bay heads into Haydock in cracking form after a tidy win at Chelmsford just eight days ago. He carries a 4lb penalty for that success but still looks fairly treated, especially considering his previous turf form. The step back up in trip should suit him well, and with confidence high, he’s got a strong chance of following up.

Unplugged returns to Haydock where he’s a two-time winner and tends to go well in these amateur races. He ran a fair race at Nottingham last time out and has dropped to a mark he’s more than capable of winning from. If they go quick early and he settles into a rhythm, he could be a big player back at a course he clearly likes.

THE DANCING POET has lost his way a touch, but is considered back on turf at last winning mark. This jock was on board when he last won at Catterick, and there's some course form in the back catalogue too. The last three runs have been too competitive at a higher grade, but he could well improve now in more suitable company.

SWIFT TUTTLE has formerly been competitive from much higher ratings on the level and this dual-purpose operator takes his chance with the yard in good form. That could be an advanatage as he lacks a recent run , but bringing course form suited by the forecast rain he could surprise.
Bit of value - not sure such long odds are deserved here - first run since October and first run for new yard, but did have two wins last year.
There may be some improvement with Hollie Doyle's mount, but at these odds, Sunlit Uplands looks as though he is ripe for stepping up in trip after some decent efforts over a furlong shorter.
Placed off this mark in his nursery over course and distance last September. Should have improved since then and has a decent chance from this mark.

One of the most experienced in the field & has won on heavy before but will probably get good / good to soft tonight . Had seasonal reappearance at Bath over 5f 30 days ago beaten 5.5L but should be fitter for that run & extra trip tonight should suit . O.Murphy booked is a positive , a negative however is draw from stall 1 hence each way tip .

L'KARAMA switches to turf ahead of handicap debut. Those fancied from the Archie Watson yard are often ridden by Hollie Doyle and this young three year old horse has shown something through qualifying. That could mean the opening mark reflects already displayed ability , but possible value found

INITIAL BLUE represents a powerful in-form southern yard who won this race last year. The booking of an also in-form Tom Marquand clearly reads well for his chance and with the benefit of a reappearance sighter behind him taking on his own age group he appeals.
Ew chance. Shaped as if this trip would suit when running on at Donny on reappearance last time. Drops a pound here and interesting jockey booking with Muscutt taking over.

Has obviously had problems in training. Only three runs. Run needed last time at Kempton, having been off 12 months. Will improve going up in distance. Yard in good form. Small each way advised, but my NAP anyway.

Homestrait has been knocking on the door with two solid second-place finishes at Beverley, both over 5 furlongs. She’s shown a good attitude and looks ready to go one better. This race doesn’t appear to have any standout contenders, so if she maintains her form, she’s got a strong chance of getting off the mark.
Ran a race full of promise in a more competitive race than this at Chester on debut and can win this with that experience.

Well worth a shot at these odds. There's not a lot in this to make it too competitive. The selection showed promise on debut last time out when 3rd at Wolverhampton. Raced wide but stayed on well that day, was an eye-catcher. No reason why he can't be involved here with improvement likely.
Star Legend has been in cracking form of late with two hurdles wins plus an easy victory on the flat at Chelmsford eight days ago.

Previous form figures of 53312 and the cheekpieces have made all the difference. He's 1lb higher here but Kaiya Fraser takes 3lb off. Return to this longer trip looks to be in his favor and still has relatively low mileage.

Stellarmasterpiece has been in cracking form at Catterick this spring, winning over 1m4f in April and then finishing a close second next time out. She’s stepping up to 1m6f today, which could bring out even more improvement. With her recent performances and a liking for the track, she looks a solid contender here.
Stand Strong showed improvement last time; is now 6 lb better off with rival; should reverse form and be competitive today.

The Irish owners were a bit surprised (as the trainer didn't know what to expect after not having her that long) how well Wee Mary ran last time out on her debut run with trainer Rebecca Menzie. She has reportedly come out of that race well 11 days ago, and providing she starts well, then a similar run here, with thumbs up today from Rebecca, would see the 3-year-old maiden get off the mark at the 7th time of asking (only 4th run on the turf).

Cheerleader caused a stir with a surprise win at Redcar, pulling clear late on to beat Wee Mary by three-quarters of a length. That was her first run for the new yard and her first outing in nine months, so there’s every chance she’ll come on for it. She’s got a 6lb penalty to shoulder now, but if she builds on that effort, she’s got a solid shout of following up.

Has had a short break, and I think it can benefit him a lot at Catterick. The jockey is claiming 3 lbs and can help this consistent sort go close today. Catterick's course is sharp and downhill, which will favor his early speed.

Writteninthestars lines up at Catterick with a bit to prove after three quiet runs last season. He’s been gelded since and makes his handicap debut off a basement mark of 45, which could bring about some improvement. With a decent draw in stall 1 and a fresh start, he might outrun his odds if he’s come on over the winter.
No comment made

May have needed the run when back from a break at Haydock (6f) on good ground in a competitive Class 5 Handicap back in April when finishing 10th of 17 to 'Bear Rock'. Having shown plenty of early speed, but back on today's easier ground could leave that form well behind with that run under her belt with regular rider Andrew Breslin back on board.

Patontheback returns to Catterick off his last winning mark, which makes him interesting. His recent form has been a bit underwhelming, including a ninth-place finish over course and distance earlier this month. However, he’s shown in the past that he can bounce back, especially when conditions suit. If he can recapture some of that earlier form, he might outrun his odds and be competitive here.

Mersea made a winning return at Newcastle and backed it up with a fair third at Southwell. She’s been freshened up and now tries turf again, which could suit. Her form looks solid and there’s still room for progress. Should be in the mix if she runs to her best. Each-way chance
I have been waiting patiently for this one to be dropped to Class 6 at this course, usually in July. But I feel at its current mark, it could outperform these odds in Class 5.
Was 3rd on debut behind the now 90-rated Shameful, who ran a cracker at Curragh last week when 2nd on handicap debut. Switched to the Bethell Yard, and this horse could be a cut above these.
Yet to win, but five times runner-up from seven starts. Can tend to pull too much but is learning and will win races, probably starting here.

Well beaten on debut but found short of room that day. Did improve on that last time out when 4th but raced too keenly and after getting hampered couldn't quite get involved. Needs to settle better here but no reason why he can't be thereabouts if doing so.

Sand Sea makes his debut here and comes from a family with sprinting ability, so the speed is likely there. He’s been working away quietly and might just need the experience, but if the market speaks in his favour, that could be a clue here.

Likes it round here, winning 3 times over course and distance, including winning this race last year. 4lb higher this time round, but has been narrowly beaten the last twice from around this mark, so he has a chance.

Keldeo heads back to Catterick where she’s already a dual course and distance winner. She’s been in solid form this spring, including a narrow third at Beverley last time out. Now racing off just 2lb higher than her last win here, she looks well treated. With her proven record at this track and current form, she’s got a strong chance of adding another win to her tally.

Looks like a typical open-looking race with most of today's field closely matched. Hopefully, this one can go very well after attracting a lot of support as a 3/1 favorite at Beverley (5f) on Good to Firm Ground in a Class 5 Handicap earlier this month, when finishing a creditable 6th of 9 to 'Ingleby Archie', with another of today's rivals, 'Keldeo', two places ahead in 3rd. Hopefully, it can come out on top today back on today's easier ground and is considerably better off with that one, with Warren Fentiman taking off a valuable 5lb. However, it could be very tight between them both on that run.

Kept on well when winning over 6 furlongs at Lingfield 10 days ago. Up 5 pounds as a consequence but 3 pounds of that is negated by the in-form Kaiya Fraser taking the reins today, who has 5 winners from 20 rides in the last 14 days. Drops in trip and every chance to complete a hat-trick.

Birkenhead ended last term with three wins, each after a bounce back reading 121013. This year, he had his first win in April and was then second at the start of this month. I think he could bounce back from that.

Barton Snow has won both his hunter chases this season, including a win here at Stratford in March and again at Cheltenham earlier this month. That is easily the best form on offer, and he can bring up the hat trick.

The model I run suggests an upset from Figaroc. This result has been driven by Figaroc having the highest RPR of the smaller 6-runner field. The official ranking leaves Figaroc relatively well placed amongst these runners and goes out carrying the joint lowest amount of initial weight on this 2m trip. Figaroc is running for the second time post a successful wind operation and has Edward Vaughan on board claiming 5 lbs relief. This brings the total weight carried by Figaroc to the joint lowest of all the runners. The model has issued a 'very low' reading, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Famous Clermont won this race last year with the same jockey Izzie Hill and should shrug off his disappointing run at Aintree last time out.

The model I run has indicated Fairly Famous can win this one. Fairly Famous lines up here with the highest RPR of this smaller 4-runner field. The official ranking is relatively middle order, which translates to a reasonable weight being carried over this 2m 6f trip. The model has issued a 'low' stake reading, which translates to a 0.75pt bet on a scale of 0-4. This is predominantly driven by the small gap back to second in the race simulation.

A past handicap chase winner who finished second in this race last year and has since finished third over this course and distance last month. Has since won a point-to-point race and could go close here at decent odds.

The model I run suggests Gracchus De Balme should win this one. Gracchus De Balme lines up here with the highest RPR of this 8-runner field, and all horses bar one carry the same initial amount of weight. Gracchus De Balme comes here in good form, having placed well in second only 28 days ago. Race fitness shouldn't be a concern given the recent run. The model has issued a 'very low' staking indicator, largely driven by the small gap back to second in the race simulation. A 'very low' staking indicator translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

LATENIGHTFUMBLE remains a low-mileage ten year old mare and she will thrive over this most extreme of distance. She has Gina Andrews in the saddle clearly a positive and selective with the races her trainer aims her for she appeals.

Loves it here over C&D in this race over the years with form figures of 1, 1, 2, PU, 5. Comes into this race on the back of a 3rd of 18 at Cheltenham last time out. The 12/1 looks good e/w value if all eight go to post.

LEARNTALOT is interesting at big odds. He won a restricted race on this card last year which reads well for his chance and he is a nine year old who will not be found wanting on stamina. In a wide open looking race where the top of the market ciould be worth opposing he could surprise.

14-year-old Pink Eyed Pedro rolled back the years a month ago when winning at Chepstow and appeared in top form. Normally a consistent sort through his career (reaching a chase mark of 142), he was well ridden by James King, who rides again here. By holding his form, he will at least make the first three home.

The model I run suggests Walkin Out should win this one. This result has been driven by Walkin Out having the second highest RPR, but the lowest official ranking by quite a way. This subsequently means Walkin Out carries the least amount of weight around this 2m 4f trip. The model has issued a 'very low' staking indicator for this, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Plenty of back form at this time of the year over the years. It is the only course and distance winner in the field, clear top across my ratings.

The model I run suggests Kings Jet can win this one. Kings Jet lines up here with by far the highest RPR of the 11-runner field. The initial weight being carried by all the horses is the same. Very decent form before taking a break, has not run in 104 days now, but if setting off well fresh and picking up from where Kings Jet left off, then can go well. The model has issued a 'moderate' reading for this one, which translates to a 1pt stake on a scale of 0-4. This is largely as a result of the reasonable value on offer here at 4s for the predicted win probability %.

I’m Spellbound stands out as the top choice for Stratford on 30th May. Boasting an impressive recent form of 111-1, ideal age of 9, and a strong trainer-jockey partnership with Gina Andrews, it leads its race with clear advantage and offers solid value at odds of 4.33.
Has to be worth an each-way bet. New stable has reinvigorated selection, who won on Hunter debut last time, having won 4 points and is thriving at the moment. Won very easily last time.
Just run twice since 2023 with one win and one time pulled up. Worth a gamble each way to see what happens here.

Trained by Pat Twomey and ridden by WJ Lee. The trainer is in great current form with an almost 50% win rate in the last 14 days. Leading handler at this course, and the jockey has a 29% career win record when riding for Twomey. Has had two races, including last time out finishing third of ten over 6 furlongs at the Curragh, when starting as 5/4 favorite. Also finished third on debut. Today's race is a lower standard.

Johnny Murtagh trains and Ben Coen rides. This beaten favorite from the last run can be of usefulness here with the possible ability to give a good account with a big run appearing. It can be a danger to all at the finish.

Naoi wil be popular with the yard in such good form but that one is very short and a better bet could be Dermot Weld's Rajala who was nibbled at in the market on debut but rather ambled out of the stalls and couldn't close the gap despite keeping on quite well. She should do better tonight.
WESTERN DREAMER drops back in trip after finishing last of 10 on debut over 1 mile at Gowran Park last week. Robbie Colgan takes the ride.

Love Me Tender has been entered up in a few races recently but pulled out late on, presumably due to the ground. He is nicely bred being by Doctor Dino and out of a good French mare who also produced the very promising Kainsbourg, trained by Gordon Elliott. He looks like he should be another winner for Willie Mullins.
First run since September. Three runs last year where had excuses the last twice. Has another inexperienced rider on top, so take a chance for each-way purposes.

The model I run suggests an upset from Mollys Dolly. This result has been driven by Mollys Dolly having the joint highest RPR of this 12-runner field. The weights being carried all look reasonably similar, but Mollys Dolly does carry the joint lowest weight here. Tries the tongue tie for the first time to aid concentration. The model has issued a 'very low' staking indicator for this as a result of the small gap back to second in the race simulation.

Sights Unseen was a close 2nd place in her last two points in October and November. She won her first race last week in a handicap hurdle over this distance under seven-pound claimer Alix Balfe. Under the same rider, she could follow up in a beginners' chase.

Stumblin In landed as the winner here as a 7/2 favorite over course and distance in second to last outing 6 weeks ago. It looks generously priced to go again here with Jack Doyle back on board for the ride like he was on that day.

Aussie Warrior has shown fair form over hurdles but was well below his best in his latest race at Fairyhouse. Now making his chase debut, which is a big step up, especially after a less encouraging run. He’s a bit of an unknown over fences, so a small each-way shot here.

John Joseph Hanlon, better known as the Shark, has mentioned numerous times his horses prefer good ground. This Roxboro River is going chasing for the first time and could warm to the bigger obstacles, giving a good account with the trainer's son Paddy in the saddle.

The model I run suggests an upset from Star In The Park. The result has been driven predominantly by Star In The Park having the second highest RPR of this 12-runner field and is not penalized for it in weights. All horses go out carrying the same initial weight, but Star In The Park has Gavin Brouder on board relieving 3 lbs. Ran very recently, so race fitness is not a concern. The model thinks this is materially mispriced and is the value play here. 21s also does offer the 'each way' angle if you prefer that betting style. The model has issued a 'very high' staking indicator for this, which translates to a 4pt bet on a scale of 0-4. This is predominantly driven by the perceived mispricing relative to the win probability %.
The grey Serienmond will take all the beating if transferring his hurdling form over fences on his first chase attempt.

The model I run suggests Wonleg can win this race. Wonleg lines up here with the highest RPR of the runners in this field. All horses go out carrying the same amount of initial weight, bar two outsiders. Wonleg is a previous distance winner over this 2m trip. Last run 22 days ago, so race fitness should not be a concern. The model has issued a 'low' staking indicator, which translates to a 0.75pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Lost his way a bit over hurdles after a promising start but may do better now switched to chasing for a yard in sparkling form.
Has run well the last two times from this mark, and his turn is near. Fifth last time in a big field handicap, he should be competitive in this.

Belardo filly trained by Jessica Harrington who won a nursery over course and distance on final start (second time in handicaps) last year. Has run prominently early in two starts back so far. Well drawn and handicapper has given her a chance. Runs off six pounds lower mark than last time in relatively weak sprint race. Stable looks on the brink of some winners (recent good seconds). Shane Foley rides.
Not bad efforts in her qualifying races by and large, best effort came under todays jockey. Feasibly treated on handicap debut here and yard in decent nick so all in all looks a decent ew bet.

Therussiancomposer didn’t run badly at Gowran but seemed to find the mile a stretch. Now dropping back in distance, which looks like a smart move. He’s got a bit to find with a few of these, but the sharper trip could help him settle and travel better. Needs a career best here to land this, but if the pace is strong and he finishes off well, there’s an outside each-way chance. Wouldn’t rule him out completely.
El Fontenaro is fancied each way here. He is down in trip here and gets Dylan Browne McMonagle aboard this evening.

Far At Sea is a 3yo filly trained by P J F Murphy. She opened on a mark of 50 after qualifying runs, then finished unplaced on her handicap debut. She then finished 3/7 in a maiden, beaten 5.25 lengths over 6f, having led into the final furlong, posting under Ben Corn (no claim) a career-high RPR of 61. The Irish handicapper harshly put up Far At Sea 13lb, and she's been disappointing in two starts since in handicaps. Consequently, she has been dropped 8lb and runs today off 49 with Wayne Hassett's 5lb claim. Today's handicap mark and 5f trip could see her to better effect at a whopping 50-1 and her pedigree suggests better being out of a dam that won three times over 6f and a fourth foal related to two individual winners who also won three times posting career high RPR of 66 and 82 over 5f .
I think that Goodie Two Shoes will prove too good for this field and win this valuable listed race for this yard. Not much else that catches the eye, bar this horse.

Huge rating, and even though favourite, still offering value on these numbers. Progressive Listed form, strong recent runs and is going up in trip which will suit his running style better. Can't see anyone bettering this horse today.

Samui is a smart gelding with two wins over longer distances last season. He showed good form recently in a Punchestown handicap hurdle, proving he’s fit and ready to go. If he brings that form back to the flat, he has a strong chance to win or place here.

Has been a much improved horse this year and coming 2nd to the now retired Kyprios last time out was a decent run. In my opinion, it could have been even better if the head-down, never-looking-where-he's-going jockey hadn't sprayed Kyprios all over the track in the final furlong. Not saying Dallas Star would have won, but it was closing when it finally got out of the way, so it would have been a lot closer. Is drifting at 9-1, but in my opinion, will see out this trip and should be competitive.

SEO LINN has won three NH flat races from 2m to 2m 1f. She was second in a NH flat race over 2m 1f at Punchestown on her latest outing last month. On the flat today, the course, distance, and going should suit her, and she could well be able to go one better and win this race.

Pleasing enough debut when finishing third in a decent race at Gowran. Couple of these have had a go in bumpers including the odds on favourite and they might find this a bit too sharp so Spring Dance looks the one to be on.

You can expect Seo Linn to be tough to beat. She's already advertised her credentials and has a win at Cheltenham and Aintree. Already at longer odds, maybe Colpe Cross can sneak a place under Wayne Lordan? The stable readied a couple last season. Hopefully, the eight runners currently remaining will go to post.

Atheneum showed little on debut, finishing third after a slow start and then missing nearly a year. Moving up in trip may suit, but with so little experience and a long break, it’s hard to be confident here, so a small each-way on this.
This looks like being an open-looking race, and I am going to side with Bowensonfire, who has been really consistent, having won or placed in the last 4 races, and will be fresh from a break.

The model I run suggests Star Official can win this race. This result has been driven by Star Official having the highest RPR of the 8 runner field. This horse also goes out with the second lowest official ranking, which translates to the second lowest weight being carried around this 2m trip. Star Official last ran 46 days ago and is a prior course and distance winner, so no concerns around ability to get the job done at this course or race fitness. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Going for the second place here (or maybe a shock). Miss Dishy showed promise with a hurdle win last October but has struggled badly in her last three runs, including her handicap debut. If she can pull the rabbit out of the hat, she may just squeak into a place here as the mark is dropping.
More than capable from this mark, same as when badly hampered last time, losing all chance. It is worth another chance here.

The model I run suggests Itsalonglongroad can win this one. This result has been driven by Itsalonglongroad having the highest RPR of the smaller 7-runner field. Itsalonglongroad has one of the lower official rankings here, meaning he looks well treated on this weight. Goes out carrying far less weight than the two current market leaders who are top of the weights. This is a weight differential of over 1 stone. Itsalonglongroad is a prior course and distance winner here and looks to get the job done again over this 1m 7.5f trip. The model has issued a 'low' staking indicator, which translates to a 0.75pt bet on a scale of 0-4. This result has been driven by the combination of a small win probability % gap back to second, but the reasonable value on offer here at 10s.

Lake Chad was a comfortable winner over course and distance last October off 105 and his handicap mark was pushed up further to 118 by winning another two mile chase at Thurles in February. He has struggled in his latest three chases over further but dropped back to the minimum distance at Tramore where he has won three chases and now on 114 he may go close again and 16-1 is a generous price.
Has now dropped to the lowest handicap mark of his career and was a very narrowly beaten runner-up at Roscommon last time out. Can go one better here.

La La Lucrative is a 4-year-old gelding trained by Matthew J Smith. He is a two-time winner and won last time out for the new yard, having left Gemma Tutty. He made all to win by 3.5 lengths under today's jockey, Robby Colgan. Despite an 8lb rise, he should put up a bold showing now dropped 1/2 furlong. That was a joint career-high RPR of 70, and he handles today's good ground.

CONVINCING has a top rider booked and he should step forward on the back of his seasonal reappearance. He makes handicap debut from what would appear a fair mark and suitably drawn for this distance he would appear to be one of the more likely types.

Colugo looks interesting on her handicap debut for a stable who had a winner last week. Unplaced in 3 starts last season, she returned in February at Dundalk when second in a maiden over 7 furlongs. She failed to build on that back there in March but possibly found the 8 furlongs trip too far. Back at 7 furlongs off a fair opening mark, she looks like a good EW bet with 4 places on offer.

Unusual to see this horse out so early in the year, but he has been hurdling recently, so that should have put him right for this. Has had a few good races with Colin Keane and has a useful piece of form at Down Royal earlier in his racing career. Looks decent each-way value.

A speculative each way is taken with Run Forrest Run, who looks on a handy mark at present. Was totally unsuited by the going on yard debut and could be in with a chance now that the blinkers are back on.

I am going to go each way, but truth be told, it's probably all or nothing with Uncle Albert. Won on heavy going and I'm not sure there will be rain to change today's going of good, but I'm also not too sure it's the going that's been the problem, it's been the mark. Competitive off opening mark of 65 in 2023 (came 2nd), then 3rd by a head off 69 and won first race of 2024 by nearly 4 lengths off 72, but has struggled ever since. If the going is a concern, they will pull him out and seasonal debut was too far and is back in trip off 66 with a decent 5lb claimer. It looks like they are trying to give him every chance, so let's hope he misses the 'open cellar door' and gets a 'hole in one.'

Well beaten at Gowran Park on stable debut nine days ago but should come on appreciably for that first outing in seven months. He's a sixteen-race maiden but showed he has ability on more than one occasion when trained by Eve Johnson Houghton. Has dropped to a career-low mark and while no more than speculative, his huge odds may represent a bit of value.
Letters Of Love improved in maiden claimed, which indicates good form. Can overcome wide draw today and has hope today. Good value pick in this race.
Found 5f too sharp when favourite last time out at Bellewstown. Trip much more suitable here. Yard could be in better form but Colin Keane sticks with him and so do I.

BREATH OF YOU ticks a few boxes in this 0/60 over 7 furlongs for 3-year-olds. Ran on late over 6 LTO at Navan, shaped like she wanted and needed further. This ex-French filly had 2 spins over a mile prior to that, and we can safely put a line through them now based on that performance at Navan. She’s down 10 lbs now after those 3 runs and has a low draw here today on ground it appears she likes, suggesting she shouldn’t be far away.

At a price here (22/1), Andy Oliver's 3-year-old gelding BAMAKO could surprise. Yes, I'm well aware this son of SANDS OF MALI finished dead last 20 days ago at Naas, but that effort came off a 218-day sabbatical and looked far too sharp over the minimum trip (5f). He should, and could, strip much fitter for that run.
If we look back at the only time this charge ran over today’s trip on turf, we see a respectable 5th place finish - beaten just 3¾ lengths - right here in County Down last June. Today represents a drop in class and he’s partnered with a top pilot in the shape of Gary Carroll. The yard is performing well, boasting a 43.75% place strike rate over the past fortnight.
A first-time visor is fitted too, which could sharpen him up further. Should this charge benefit from last time out’s pipe-opener and given his prior experience over this trip and uphill finish, I’m happy to take a punt.

MICASO was one of only two horses from single-digit draws to finish in the first nine at Navan earlier this month but was seen running on well over six furlongs. He apparently has a good high draw from stall fourteen today, plus the added bonus of an extra furlong to race over, which should suit.
Consistent mare has been placed on 5 of her 6 outings in bumpers. Reported to have schooled well and step up in trip should suit for hurdles debut.
Softening of the ground won't harm her chances. A little disappointing last time on faster ground, but could bounce back here with conditions to suit.
Finished second in a point-to-point last month before joining current connections. Looks interesting on breeding and could be one to note making race debut under rules.
Drops back into maiden company, having been unlucky in his last two runs, both in handicaps and suffering trouble in running both times. A clear run here sees him win.
Summer Island improved on better ground last time. Up in trip today and may continue progression with conditions in her favor.

The price of this has just jumped up to 25-1, which I am very happy about. I think this horse is a lot better than results have shown. It was very wide last time out over this distance, and the jockey seemed to not handle the horse, who I believe was a claimer. Egan gets the ride today, who will hopefully give it the ride it deserves. If these odds suddenly drop, I'd get on quick.

Minella Boss ran 3 times last season on unsuitable ground of which is proven when looking into its Golden Horn pedigree who always won on good racing ground. Nothing with soft in the ground condition. Has had a run this season on soft again to clear the cob weds off for todays race on good ground. Todays joc getting the leg up first time is the best around this track. This horse is 5/1 in places was 33/1 when last seen so somebody knows something. e/w profit is guaranteed at 15/2.

Ran very green on debut but the penny dropped and this Churchill colt finished the race nicely. Not so good on boggy ground last time out but can get back on track on a sounder surface here for his local yard.
Steps up in trip here, which will suit. Billy Lee booked and wearing new headgear for the first time. Is worth backing each way in the hope she is not prepping for handicaps.

An eye-catcher last time out at Cork, staying on strongly from off the pace and now upped in trip further. Hopefully, ridden slightly more aggressively, can go even closer today with the talented claimer Harney in the plate taking off 7lb.

I’m taking a chance on Sean Aherne’s THE BORDER BOY here. It’s a sea of duck eggs, but the added first-time cheekpieces might bring out that bit of improvement required. His best snippet of form was here in this race last year, finished 5th, beaten 5 lengths off 86. Off 74 today and a run under his belt, he should be strip fitter. Not one to get overly confident in, I understand, but has shown a liking for the track and now 12 lbs better off.
BEECHROAD WINNIE was beaten just 3 lengths over C&D last June after a similar layoff; capable of going well fresh and worth a second look.

I'll be honest??'I'm looking for a BIG-priced potential improver here, and while trainer John Flavin's 6-year-old gelding AG OBAIR GO CRUA has shown some progress, the bar was low considering he pulled up on his previous two runs. Both were on soft ground, though, so we’ll (grudgingly) forgive. Back from a 118-day break 16 days ago at Tipperary (25f, good), this son of MAHLER finished 11th, but around the 21??'22f mark he wasn’t completely tailed off. So, this drop back to 21¾f might just be more his thing.
He’s now 10lbs down from his first handicap run, including today’s 3lb dip??'which doesn’t hurt. The one real positive? The booking of top pro Darragh O’Keeffe. That’s a major upgrade (and I say that as a Tiernan Power Roche fan). O’Keeffe arrives in red-hot form??'21.62% win and 42.54% place strike rate over the past fortnight, with a 32.46% place strike here at Tramore over the last five years. Even better? A 50% place rate when riding for Flavin in the past year, and Flavin himself has a tidy 40% place strike at Tramore.
This should really be a watching brief??'but if you're joining me, check if your bookie accepts payment in buttons.

Dee's Getaway did not take to chasing well on last three starts but a repeat of her form over CD when winning a maiden hurdle in September last year would see her go close in this. With quick ground and the smaller obstacles it would be no surprise to see her at least make the frame here.

This is a fairly low-grade 0-100 handicap hurdle and suited to an unexposed type. Menas Miracle fits that bill. She makes her handicap debut off a mark of 75 and carries 10 stone 3 pounds. Conor Stone-Walsh claims a 3 lbs allowance for trainer Brendan Walsh. 6-year-old by Jet Away (good source of hurdles winners). Cosy 13-length winner of a 3 miles Point in December (not so long ago). That ability has not been on display in a bumper and three maiden hurdles since. I expect the mare will show a lot more this evening.

Nevereverever had a poor run last time at Tipperary, finishing well down the field. That effort was disappointing and needs to be put behind him. If he can bounce back to his better form, there’s a chance he could be competitive and he can be an each-way chance today.

YORKSHIRE ESCAPE runs for a top yard and is clearly well handicapped. She can sometimes have her own ideas about this game , but if she turns up in the right frame of mind and consents to compete then she could be dangerous.

Maughreen is a 6-year-old daughter of Walk In The Park ex Molly's Mate. She won her bumper on her debut outing at 1/2f by 11l at Punchestown in January '24. That bumper produced seven winners from four runners. She then won her 2m3f mares maiden hurdle at 4/11f, also at Punchestown, in January '25. That hurdle race produced three winners from two runners. She runs here off a mark of 123 in this mares hurdle where she'll be ridden by P Townend for WP Mullins. Last time out, she was unplaced at 12/1 in a 2m4f Grade 1 hurdle at Fairyhouse last month. She drops in class and distance here, and I make her my Nap of the day.

Liadawn is a grey 5-year-old daughter of Jukebox Jury ex Snag List. She makes her racecourse debut in this mares' bumper. She'll be ridden by Mr. P.W. Mullins for his father W.P. Mullins. She's one for your horse tracker. The stable is in top form at the moment. I think she can open her account here.
